title: L15 · Endocrine System
subtitle: Glands, hormone types, and each hormone's source, target and effect

lines.text: The endocrine system controls the body with hormones.
An **endocrine gland** has no ducts. It releases hormones into the blood.
A **hormone** is a chemical messenger.
Its **target tissue** is the organ or cell it affects.
For each hormone, know its source, target and effect.
**Humoral**: a change in blood levels, like calcium.
**Neural**: a nerve signal, like the sympathetic system on the adrenal medulla.
**Hormonal**: another hormone, like the hypothalamus signaling the pituitary.
**Steroid** hormones are made from cholesterol. They pass through the membrane and activate genes directly.
Estrogen, progesterone, testosterone and the corticosteroids.
**Biogenic amines** are modified amino acids. Epinephrine, thyroid hormone, melatonin.
**Protein** hormones are most hormones. They can't cross the membrane, so they use a second messenger.
The pituitary is pea sized. It sits in the **sella turcica**, below the hypothalamus.
The **anterior pituitary** makes and releases its own hormones.
The **posterior pituitary** stores and releases hormones made by the hypothalamus.
**Growth hormone** targets all cells, especially muscle and bone. It increases body size.
Too much in childhood is gigantism. In adults it's acromegaly.
**Prolactin** targets the mammary glands. It makes milk.
**TSH** targets the thyroid. It releases thyroid hormone.
**ACTH** targets the adrenal cortex. It releases glucocorticoids.
**FSH** targets the gonads. It develops eggs and sperm.
**LH** triggers ovulation, and testosterone release in men.
Together they are the gonadotropins.
Melanocyte stimulating hormone has little effect in humans.
**ADH**, antidiuretic hormone, targets the kidneys.
Anti means against. Diuretic means urination. It holds water and raises blood pressure.
Too little causes diabetes insipidus.
**Oxytocin** targets the uterus and mammary glands. Contractions in birth, and milk release.
The pineal gland sits deep in the brain. Light affects it.
It releases **melatonin**.
Melatonin sets the **circadian rhythm**, the daily sleep cycle.
The thyroid is butterfly shaped, just below the larynx.
**Thyroid hormone**, T3 and T4, targets every cell. It's the main metabolic hormone.
Too much is **Graves'** disease. Too little can cause a **goiter**.
**Calcitonin** targets bone. It lowers blood calcium.
Four parathyroid nodules sit on the back of the thyroid.
**PTH** targets bone and kidney. It raises blood calcium.
It's the antagonist of calcitonin.
The thymus sits in front of the heart. It shrinks after puberty.
**Thymosin** matures T lymphocytes.
The adrenal glands sit on top of the kidneys.
The inner medulla responds to the sympathetic nervous system.
It releases **epinephrine** and **norepinephrine**.
Heart rate, blood pressure and blood sugar rise. Airways open.
The cortex has three zones. Glomerulosa, fasciculata, reticularis.
**Aldosterone** targets the kidney. It holds sodium and releases potassium.
**Cortisol** raises blood sugar to resist stress.
**Androgens** are made in small amounts.
Too little cortex hormone is Addison's. Too much cortisol is Cushing's.
When oxygen is low, the kidneys release **EPO**, erythropoietin.
It tells red bone marrow to make more red blood cells.
When blood pressure or sodium drops, the kidneys release **renin**.
That starts the renin angiotensin aldosterone system, which raises blood pressure.
The pancreas is mostly exocrine. Its **islets** of Langerhans are endocrine.
Alpha cells release **glucagon**. It raises blood sugar.
Beta cells release **insulin**. It lowers blood sugar.
Type 1 diabetes: no insulin. Type 2: cells don't respond to it.
The ovaries release **estrogen** and **progesterone**.
Both grow the uterine lining. Progesterone maintains pregnancy.
The testes release **testosterone**.
It matures the male reproductive system.
